evals.name: spec-overdue-tickets
evals.prompt: First run `bash /Users/dmitri/dev/swd-skills/evals/spec/make_fixture.sh OUTPUT_DIR/repo`, then work inside OUTPUT_DIR/repo. Spec this out before anyone plans or builds it: support agents want tickets that pass their due time to show as OVERDUE in `ticketdesk list`, and a new `ticketdesk overdue` command that lists only overdue tickets, oldest due first. Write the spec into the repo's docs the way the repo does specs. Nobody is available to answer questions during this run: where the skill would ask me, write the questions to OUTPUT_DIR/questions.md, state the assumption you proceed on, and continue. Do not change any code. Do not commit.
evals.expected_output: A new or amended spec file under docs/product-specs/ following the repo's own convention: an intro, a Prefix line, non-goals, at least five criteria headed PREFIX-NNN with testable behavioral bodies including edge and error cases (closed tickets, nothing overdue, a ticket exactly at its due time), feature-local invariants referencing INV-001 and INV-002 so overdue is derived and never written to the log, the product-specs README index and prefix table updated, open questions listed, lint-clean prose, no code changed.
assertions: A spec for the overdue feature exists under OUTPUT_DIR/repo/docs/product-specs/, either as a new file with a new prefix or as new criteria appended to tickets.md or cli.md with fresh IDs; the transcript or spec says which was chosen and why.

The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).

At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.

Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.

The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.

The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.

docs/product-specs/README.md is updated: the new file appears in the prefix table and the index with a one-line summary (or, if criteria were appended to an existing file, the README needed no change and the spec says so).
Open questions are listed at the end of the spec (or in OUTPUT_DIR/questions.md) and assumptions are marked inline; none of them is silently resolved in a criterion.
Running `python3 /Users/dmitri/dev/swd-skills/scripts/prose-lint.py` on the new or changed spec file(s) reports 0 findings.
Skim test: the intro paragraph's first sentence says what the feature is for a support agent; each criterion title names the behavior; no lead is a teaser or a qualifier chain.

`git status --porcelain` in OUTPUT_DIR/repo shows changes only under docs/ and to AGENTS.md (the repo's own docs/README.md asks for its index to be updated); nothing committed; ticketdesk/ and tests/ are untouched.
